messages.content: 計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
**標準誤（Standard Error）**

對於樣本平均值 \(\bar{x}=98.2\)、樣本標準差 \(s=1.4\)、樣本大小 \(n=40\)，其標準誤（即抽樣分布的標準差）計算如下：

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.2215
\]

---

如果你想進一步做零假設檢定（\(H_0:\mu=98.6\)），可以計算 t 統計量：

\[
t = \frac{\bar{x}-\mu_0}{SE} = \frac{98.2-98.6}{0.2215} \approx -1.805
\]

對應的雙尾 p 值約為 **0.075**（使用自由度 \(df=n-1=39\) 的 t 分布）。這表示在常見的顯著水準（如 0.05）下，無法拒絕零假設。

The phrase "零假設檢定的標準差" might refer to the standard error of the mean under null? Actually "標準差" could be "standard deviation". But they already gave sample standard deviation. They might want the standard error of the mean: SE = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). That would be 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean under null? That is same as SE. So answer: 0.2215.

But maybe they want the p-value? The phrase "零假設檢定的標準差" is ambiguous. Let's interpret: They want to compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean (i.e., standard error) for the null hypothesis test. So we can provide that.

Alternatively, they might want to compute the t-statistic and then p-value. But the question explicitly says "計算...的標準差". So likely just standard error.

Thus answer: Standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 0.2215.

We can also mention that if we want to test H0: μ=98.6 vs Ha: μ≠98.6, we compute t = (98.2 - 98.6) / (1.4 / sqrt(40)) = (-0.4) / 0.2215 ≈ -1.805. Then p-value two-tailed ~ 0.075. But the question didn't ask for p-value. But we can provide it anyway.
